title: The Lost Ten Tribes: Where Did They Go?
author: QUILL
notes: Modern descent claims are framed as claims. Sargon II figure given as 'about 27,000'. Not-proven line in beat 11.

beats.text: Ten tribes of Israel vanished. Where did they go?
Assyria conquers Samaria, capital of the northern kingdom.
beats.say: Assyria conquers Suh-MARE-ee-uh, capital of the northern kingdom.

beats.text: Sargon II's own records boast of deporting about 27,000 people.
beats.say: SAR-gon the Second's own records boast of deporting about twenty-seven thousand people.

beats.text: Second Kings says they were settled in Halah, and by the Habor river in Gozan.
beats.say: Second Kings says they were settled in HAY-lah, and by the HAY-bor river in GO-zan.

beats.text: Others went to the cities of the Medes, in what is now Iran.
beats.say: Others went to the cities of the MEEDS, in what is now Iran.

beats.text: Deportation was Assyrian policy, and foreign peoples were moved into Samaria.
beats.label: DEPORTED

beats.text: Yet some northerners remained: Hezekiah later invited them to Passover.
beats.say: Yet some northerners remained: Hez-eh-KY-ah later invited them to Passover.

beats.text: The Bnei Menashe of northeast India say they descend from Manasseh.
beats.say: The BNAY men-NAH-sheh of northeast India say they descend from Manasseh.

beats.text: Some Pashtun traditions claim Israelite roots, but most scholars doubt it.
beats.say: Some PUSH-toon traditions claim Israelite roots, but most scholars doubt it.

beats.text: Britain, India, Afghanistan: loud claims, but no proof.
beats.label: CLAIMS VS PROOF
beats.source: claims (British Israelism; Bnei Menashe; Pashtun tradition)

beats.text: Plainly: no modern group has been proven to descend from them.
From Samaria to Media, the written trail goes cold.
beats.say: From Suh-MARE-ee-uh to MEE-dee-uh, the written trail goes cold.

beats.text: So where do you think the ten tribes went?
